public_rationale: The claim has two parts. The first part, that OpenAI's lead was slipping, holds. Menlo Ventures found OpenAI's enterprise API share fell to 27%, behind Anthropic's 40% (e1). Similarweb showed ChatGPT's share of chatbot web traffic falling from about 86% to about 65% as Gemini grew (e2). The second part, that OpenAI's financing was slipping, does not hold on the evidence from the time. Nvidia's $100 billion plan had stalled (e3). But Nvidia's CEO said it would still make what could be its largest investment ever in OpenAI's current round (e4). SoftBank was reported in talks to add $30 billion to a round of up to $100 billion (e5). Two weeks after the post, that round was announced at $110 billion. So the lead part holds and the financing part fails.
limitations: 'Lead' was measured by market share, not by benchmark quality.
The financing part is hedged ('it looks'), and the signs at the time pointed both ways.
The round announced on Feb 27 falls outside the target period, so it serves only as context.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's competitive lead is slipping and its financing appears to be slipping too.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI’s lead is slipping, and now it looks their financing is, too.

from_speaker: now it looks their financing is, too
our_interpretation: Lead slipping: in the months before the post, OpenAI's share of usage or of the market was falling as rivals gained.
Financing slipping: around the post date, OpenAI's ability to line up new money was weakening, for example backers withdrawing or rounds stalling.
The two parts are judged separately.
criteria.support_condition: Data showing OpenAI losing share to rivals in late 2025 or early 2026, plus reports from the same period of investors withdrawing or a stalled round.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Data showing OpenAI holding its share, or reports from the same period that major investors were lining up new money for a large round.
